description: List jobs, optionally filtered by work status, scheduled date range, customer, or assigned technician. Each row carries an employees field - the technicians assigned to that job, with id and name - so who is on a job is read off the row rather than assumed. Rows also carry on_my_way_at and started_at, which are how a job being worked right now shows itself. Rows carrying a deleted_at value are deleted jobs - exclude them from counts and revenue. Every row also carries lead_source, the channel the job came in through ("Online Booking", "Reserve with Google", a source the office picked, or absent when none was recorded) - so which jobs were booked online is read off this one listing, never by fetching each job in turn. Times come back twice: scheduled_start/scheduled_end in UTC, and scheduled_start_local/scheduled_end_local already rendered in the account's own zone. Quote the local ones to a person.

customer_id.description: Only jobs for this customer id

employee.description: Keep only jobs assigned to this technician - an employee id (from hcp_list_employees), or part of a name, matched case-insensitively against each row's employees. Housecall Pro has no employee filter on this endpoint, so this narrows the rows the OTHER filters returned, page by page: pair it with a tight scheduled window (and raise page_size) or a technician's job can sit on a page you never fetched. The reported totals count the rows before this filter.

include_attachments.description: Include each job's files with signed download links. This is the only way to reach attachments in bulk.

scheduled_start_max.description: ISO date/datetime upper bound for the scheduled start. Use the same local offset as scheduled_start_min, e.g. 2026-08-14T00:00:00-04:00 for the end of a local day.

scheduled_start_min.description: ISO date/datetime lower bound for the scheduled start. Pass your own local offset, e.g. 2026-08-13T00:00:00-04:00, not a bare UTC day: a UTC window against a business running in a local timezone shifts the day, so an evening job falls outside "today" and a late job from the day before falls inside it.

work_status.description: Filter by one or more statuses (server-side)

name: hcp_list_jobs
